questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How sad films are made to make audiences cry
Why young babies cry so often during the night
Why we cry, and differences in who cries and where
How to stop yourself crying at work or in meetings
questions.why: Neil says they'll investigate why we cry and differences between men and women, public and private.

options: At work last month after a meeting
Watching a dramatic film last week
Listening to sad music in the car
Cutting onions for dinner at home
questions.why: Sam says he burst out crying last week watching a really dramatic film.

questions.q: What does Sam think of Neil's claim that “men don't cry”?
options: He agrees completely
He thinks it is scientifically proven
He thinks it's funny but true
He thinks it's a stereotype
questions.why: Sam says, “That's a bit stereotypical, isn't it?”

questions.q: Apart from pain, what else can make people cry, according to Sam?
options: Joy, or being moved by beautiful music or art
Feeling hungry or thirsty after a long day
Being very tired after not sleeping enough
Hearing a joke that is funny but also sad
questions.why: Sam says we also cry to show joy and when moved by something beautiful like music or a painting.

questions.q: What seems to be true about men and crying in public?
options: They never do it
They do it more often than women
They feel less embarrassed about it
They only do it at work
questions.why: Neil says while men cry less often, they seem to feel less embarrassed about crying in public.

questions.q: According to Joanna Cross, what is the risk of crying regularly at work?
options: You may lose your job immediately without warning
Your colleagues may start crying in the office too
You may be given more work to keep you busy
You may not be taken seriously or may get a label
questions.why: She says they might not be taken so seriously when something matters, or they get a label.

questions.q: Why does Joanna Cross mention being asked to make a cup of tea?
options: To show that a cup of tea helps people calm down
A small request can be the last straw after problems
As an example of bosses treating women unfairly
To show that crying is always about big problems
questions.why: She says after built-up resentments, a simple request can make you weep; it's a backlog of situations.

questions.q: What does Sam jokingly say used to make him cry at work?
options: Neil's onion sandwiches
Neil's quiz questions
Sad news stories
Long meetings
questions.why: He says the only time he cries at work is when Neil used to bring in onion sandwiches.
